diagnosis_explanation:
Your lungs have a type of pneumonia. Pneumonia is an infection in the lungs. This type of pneumonia is not typical. Doctors suspect a virus caused it.

Your body did not have enough oxygen. This is called hypoxia.

You have rheumatoid arthritis. This is a condition that causes joint pain and swelling.

Doctors also suspect you have mild stress-induced adrenal insufficiency. This means your body may not make enough of certain hormones when under stress.
medication_rationale:
Rocephin 1 g daily:
This medicine is an antibiotic. It fights infections caused by certain germs. It was prescribed to help treat your pneumonia. You may have some redness or swelling where it is given. Call your doctor if you get a rash, or have trouble breathing.

Azithromycin:
This medicine is an antibiotic. It helps fight infections caused by germs. You were told to finish the rest of your pills. You may have an upset stomach or diarrhea. Call your doctor if you get a severe rash or have trouble breathing.

Prednisone 20 mg per day:
This medicine is a steroid. It can help lower swelling in your body. It is used to help with your pneumonia. You might feel more hungry or have trouble sleeping. Call your doctor if you have vision changes or mood changes.

Methotrexate every week:
This medicine calms down your body's defense system. It is used for ongoing health problems. You may feel tired or have an upset stomach. Call your doctor if you have mouth sores or bleeding.

Remicade every eight weeks:
This medicine calms down your body's defense system. It helps with ongoing health problems. You may feel tired or get headaches. Call your doctor if you get a fever or a new rash.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and weak. This is normal.
- Rest as much as possible.
- You may have a mild cough.
- Eat bland foods if your stomach feels upset.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.
- Your goal this week is to rest and stay hydrated.

**Week 2:**
- You may start to feel a little more energy.
- Shortness of breath when moving around should slowly lessen.
- Drink plenty of fluids like water or clear broth.
- Avoid anything that makes your cough worse.
- Call your doctor if your cough gets much worse.
- Your goal this week is to walk short distances inside your home.

**Week 3:**
- You can try doing light chores if you feel up to it.
- Avoid any strenuous activity or heavy lifting.
- Listen to your body and rest when you need to.
- Eat regular meals to help your body heal.
- Call your doctor if you develop a fever again.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes twice a day.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel stronger and have more energy.
- You can slowly increase your activity level.
- Avoid returning to very hard work or exercise too soon.
- Continue to eat healthy foods to support recovery.
- Call your doctor if you have chest pain when you cough.
- Your goal this week is to walk outside for 15 minutes.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Feeling better can take several weeks.
- Keep resting and slowly increase your activity.
- Eat well and drink plenty of fluids.
- Recovery is a gradual process.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- You cannot catch your breath: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Chest pain that will not stop: Your heart needs help now.
- Uncontrolled bleeding that won't stop: Get help right away.
- Face drooping or arm weakness: These are stroke signs. Minutes matter.
- Loss of consciousness or fainting: Get help right away.
- Seizure: Get help right away.
- Severe allergic reaction: Get help right away.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever above 101 degrees F: You may have an infection.
- Confusion or disorientation: This could be serious.
- Cannot keep fluids down: You need fluids now.
- Severe pain that medicine does not help: Seek help now.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild redness of the wound: This can happen while you heal.
- Mild swelling without pain: This can happen while you heal.
- Fatigue that is improving: You are getting better.
- Questions about your medicine: Your doctor can help you.
